standfirst: A burnt out webtoon producer subscribes to a virtual boyfriend service and gets a rotating cast of famous faces. The premise is the most current thing in Korean romance this year and the show does almost nothing with it: no escalation, no cost, no argument about what she is actually buying. If what you wanted was the light fantasy romance it promises rather than the one it delivers, these are the better versions of the same evening.

picks.why: The same job, done with more charm and a similar collapse. A workplace lie, a fake relationship, two leads with actual chemistry, and a first episode that sets a bar the rest of the run cannot clear. Difference: the lie has consequences here and the office politics are real for a while, so the middle section has stakes that Boyfriend on Demand never bothers to create.

For the low effort, high comfort register: a teacher starting over in a small town and a man who will not stop bothering her. Same absence of jeopardy, better use of it. Difference: it takes four episodes to find its footing and then holds a full point higher for the rest of the run, so the shape is the opposite of this one, which peaks in its first hour.

The other 2025 fantasy romance about getting exactly what you asked for. A wish granting premise with clear rules, a cold woman who wants nothing, and a lead who is the fantasy object by design. Difference: it commits to the cost of the wish, which is the whole thing Boyfriend on Demand refuses to do, and its ending asks you to accept a real loss.

If the appeal was the parade of tropes at speed. Fake dating, a workplace secret, cartoon logic, and a supporting couple carrying half the episodes. Same disposable pleasure. Difference: it is genuinely funny, which is the one resource Boyfriend on Demand does not have, and it never asks to be taken seriously for a second.

The straight romcom that everything in this neighbourhood is imitating. Two leads with immaculate timing, an office, a contract, no fantasy machinery required. Difference: it is a two hander with a thin ensemble, so it lives or dies on the leads, and both of them are far better matched than the subscription cast here.

The original template for a famous woman falling for an impossible man. Same wish fulfilment engine, executed when the format was still new. Difference: it is twenty one episodes long with a melodrama plot and a deadline attached, so the fantasy has weight and an ending that costs something.

against.title: Lovely Runner
against.why: The default pick for anything with a fantasy romance premise and a huge cast of cameos. It works because it has a deadline and a real fear underneath it. Boyfriend on Demand has no clock and no threat, so anyone arriving here from Lovely Runner will spend ten hours waiting for the plot to start.

against.title: True Beauty
against.why: Paired for the glossy surface, and the two barely overlap. That one is a teen romance about appearance with a love triangle at its centre, pitched at high school and written for it. This is an adult professional in an apartment with a device. Nothing in the emotional register matches.

against.title: Nevertheless
against.why: Suggested as the other beautiful, low plot romance. It is a deliberately uncomfortable study of a bad relationship, shot like a perfume advert, and it is not remotely light. If you wanted the frictionless fantasy this show sells, Nevertheless is the opposite experience.
